title: Coherent finite-free coefficient comparison for ambient derived direct image
statement:
Let $q:Z\to W$ be a morphism of schemes, using small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $T=Z,W$, let $R_T\to S_T$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings, with specified isomorphisms $q^{-1}R_W\cong R_Z$ and $q^{-1}S_W\cong S_Z$ commuting with these maps. Suppose $S_W$ is finite free as an $R_W$-module sheaf, meaning $S_W\cong R_W^{\oplus d}$ for some finite integer $d\geq0$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(R_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ and $D(S_T)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], canonical module pullback/direct-image adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $C_T(M)=M\otimes^L_{R_T}S_T$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $\mu:Lq_S^*C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}C_ZLq_R^*$ be the canonical balancing comparison of derived pullback and scalar tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For $M\in D(R_Z)$ define
$$\pi_{S/R,q,M}:C_WRq_{*,R}M\longrightarrow Rq_{*,S}C_ZM$$
to be the $Lq_S^*\dashv Rq_{*,S}$-adjunct of
$$Lq_S^*C_WRq_{*,R}M\xrightarrow{\mu}C_ZLq_R^*Rq_{*,R}M\xrightarrow{C_Z(\varepsilon_{R,M})}C_ZM.$$
Then $\pi_{S/R,q}$ is a natural isomorphism of exact functors $D(R_Z)\to D(S_W)$, including compatibility with the canonical cochain shift in the input $M$. In particular this is an equality of $S_W$-module derived morphisms, not just an equality after forgetting scalars.

For identity coefficient maps $R_T\to R_T$, it is the identity under the multiplication identifications. More generally let $R_T\to S_T\to B_T$ be a further compatible tower of ring sheaves, with $q^{-1}B_W\cong B_Z$, $B_W$ finite free over $S_W$, and all inverse-image identifications commuting with the coefficient maps. Write $C_{S/R,T},C_{B/S,T},C_{B/R,T}$ for the scalar functors and $a_T:C_{B/S,T}C_{S/R,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{B/R,T}$ for balanced associativity. For every $M\in D(R_Z)$ one has
$$\pi_{B/R,q,M}=Rq_{*,B}(a_{Z,M})\,\pi_{B/S,q,C_{S/R,Z}M}\,C_{B/S,W}(\pi_{S/R,q,M})\,(a_{W,Rq_{*,R}M})^{-1}.$$
No completeness, constructibility, properness or base-field hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula (finite-free case); the input-shift and successive-coefficient equations are agent-extracted from the counit-tensor construction, not quoted as clauses of the Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Write $L_R=Lq_R^*$, $R_R=Rq_{*,R}$, and similarly for $S$. Choose an $R_W$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $S_W$. Exact identified-coefficient inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] pulls this to an $R_Z$-basis of $S_Z$. For either $T$, the maps $N^{\oplus d}\to\operatorname{Res}(N\otimes_{R_T}S_T)$, $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_i x_i\otimes e_i$, and $x\otimes\sum_i r_i e_i\mapsto(r_i x)_i$ are inverse: the tensor balancing relations prove both composites are identities. They define sheaf maps by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Kernels and cokernels of module sheaves have the underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; thus this finite-sum description proves scalar extension exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] its termwise functor computes its left derived functor on every complex, so it computes precisely $C_T$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with the stated target-ring action. The same coordinate maps give $\operatorname{Res}C_TN\cong N^{\oplus d}$ on the unbounded derived categories. If $d=0$, these are the unique maps between zero objects.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula, finite-free reduction; coordinate calculation of exact scalar extension

proof.text: Normalize $\mu:L_SC_W\cong C_ZL_R$ on the exact complex functors of Step 1. On inverse-image local tensor generators it sends $q^{-1}(x\otimes s)$ to $q^{-1}x\otimes c_S(q^{-1}s)$; its inverse is the reverse balanced map. Compatibility of $c_R,c_S$ with the coefficient map makes these maps balanced and $S_Z$-linear. They commute with restrictions, differentials and morphisms by the sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and identified-coefficient pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The exact-functor shift comparisons are degreewise identities [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; consequently these maps commute with shift, including the negative shifted differential. Localization lifts these natural isomorphisms and their equations uniquely [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. This lift is the canonical derived balancing comparison used in the statement: on a flat K-flat representative, which exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], it is the same balanced pullback map computing the scalar functors [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. No assertion about equality of derived morphisms is inferred merely by forgetting their $S$-actions.

source.place: Tags 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; normalization and input shift of balancing

proof.text:
For a tower $R\to S\to B$, choosing bases gives a basis $e_i f_j$ of $B$ over $R$, so all three scalar functors are exact by Step 1. Write $a_T:C_{B/S,T}C_{S/R,T}\cong C_{B/R,T}$. By [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], it is represented by $(x\otimes s)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\overline{s}b$. The two composites from $L_BC_{B/S,W}C_{S/R,W}$ to $C_{B/R,Z}L_R$ send every local generator $q^{-1}((x\otimes s)\otimes b)$ to $q^{-1}x\otimes c_B(q^{-1}(\overline{s}b))$: the other route gives $q^{-1}x\otimes\overline{c_S(q^{-1}s)}c_B(q^{-1}b)$, the same by the ring-square hypothesis. Tensor balancing and sheafification make this equality of $B_Z$-linear complex maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Uniqueness of localization lifts [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives
$$\mu^{B/R}L_B(a_W)=(a_ZL_R)\,C_{B/S,Z}(\mu^{S/R})\,(\mu^{B/S}C_{S/R,W}).$$
For an identity coefficient map the balanced formula is multiplication $x\otimes r\mapsto rx$, so $\mu$ becomes the identity under the unit identifications. This calculation concerns only the exact left functors; no direct-image comparison is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; elementary balancing equation for the coefficient tower and identity

proof.text: The square $\mu:L_SC_W\to C_ZL_R$ has mate $C_WR_R\to R_SC_Z$. By the explicit mate formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] this mate has transpose $C_Z(\varepsilon_R)\mu_{R_R(-)}$, exactly the defining transpose of $\pi$; hence it is $\pi$. In particular it is a natural transformation. Both scalar functors are exact by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and both derived direct images are exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so its source and target are exact functors. All four corners here are the module derived categories, and the Hom bijection used to define each component has target $D(S_W)$. Thus every component is an $S_W$-module derived morphism.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; naturality from the mate definition

proof.text:
Let $r_T:D(S_T)\to D(R_T)$ be scalar restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with the given compatible ring identifications; it supplies $b:r_ZL_S\cong L_Rr_W$, $d:r_WR_S\cong R_Rr_Z$, and conservativity of $r_W$. Put $t_M=C_Z(\varepsilon_{R,M})\mu_{R_RM}$. Its adjunct is $\pi_M$. The cited adjunct identity says that $d_{C_ZM}r_W(\pi_M)$ is the $R$-adjunct of $r_Z(t_M)b_{C_WR_RM}^{-1}$. By the balanced formula of Step 2 and the bases of Step 1, this latter morphism is
$$L_R((R_RM)^{\oplus d})\cong(L_RR_RM)^{\oplus d}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{R,M}^{\oplus d}}M^{\oplus d}.$$
Indeed its restriction to the $i$th summand sends $x\otimes e_i$ to $\varepsilon_{R,M}(x)\otimes e_i$. This identifies the actual restricted comparison, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of its source and target.

source.place: Tags 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; scalar-restriction adjunct identity

proof.text: Let $\iota_i:M\to M^{\oplus d}$ and $p_i:M^{\oplus d}\to M$ be the coordinate inclusions and projections. The adjunct of $\iota_i\varepsilon_{R,M}:L_RR_RM\to M^{\oplus d}$ is $R_R(\iota_i)$ by naturality of the adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Therefore Step 5 identifies $d\,r_W(\pi_M)$ with the map $\theta:(R_RM)^{\oplus d}\to R_R(M^{\oplus d})$ having columns $R_R(\iota_i)$. The map $(R_R(p_i))_i$ is an isomorphism because $R_R$ is a right adjoint and preserves the finite product [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits]; finite sums in these additive derived categories are also products [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its composite with $\theta$ has $(j,i)$ entry $R_R(p_j\iota_i)=\delta_{ij}$, since $R_R$ is additive [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Thus $\theta$ is its inverse. For $d=0$ the same assertion is preservation of the terminal zero object. Hence $r_W(\pi_M)$ is invertible, and conservativity in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] proves $\pi_M$ invertible in $D(S_W)$. The basis has proved invertibility of the canonical map, without entering its definition.

source.place: Tag 0944, lemma-projection-formula, final finite-free case; Categories Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact

proof.text:
For the input shift, expand the mate formula of Step 4 as
$$\pi_M=R_S(C_Z\varepsilon_{R,M})\,R_S(\mu_{R_RM})\,\eta^S_{C_WR_RM}.$$
The units and counits of $L_R\dashv R_R$ and $L_S\dashv R_S$ commute with their canonical shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]. These canonical shifts of $L_R,L_S$ are the termwise ones used above: for a K-flat resolution $P\to K$, $P[1]\to K[1]$ is one, and $q^*(P[1])=(q^*P)[1]$ degreewise, so by the representation of $Lq^*$ by $q^*P$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] the shift of resolutions and the exact-functor comparison $\tau$ agree; the shifts of $R_R,R_S$ are then the unique ones compatible with the units. The scalar functors carry the termwise shift comparisons of Step 1, by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and $\mu$ respects them by Step 2. Whiskering and composing such transformations preserves shift compatibility by [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Applied to the displayed formula this gives, with the composite shift comparisons $s_F,s_G$,
$$s_G\pi_{M[1]}=\pi_M[1]s_F$$
in $D(S_W)$. Together with Steps 4 and 6 this makes $\pi$ a natural isomorphism of exact functors, including the connecting morphisms of distinguished triangles.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; input-shift equation expanded from the adjunction formula

proof.text: For identity coefficients identify $C_W,C_Z$ with identity functors by multiplication. Step 3 identifies the coefficient square with $\mathrm{id}_{L_R}$. Its mate is $\mathrm{id}_{R_R}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause (4). Write $m_T:C_T\cong\mathrm{id}$ for these multiplication isomorphisms. Transporting a square along $m_W$ on its source and $m_Z$ on its target changes its mate by precomposition with $m_W^{-1}R_R$ and postcomposition with $R_R(m_Z)$, by naturality of the adjunction bijection [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], exactly as in Step 9. Hence Step 4 gives $R_R(m_{Z,M})\,\pi_{R/R,q,M}\,m_{W,R_RM}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{R_RM}$: $\pi_{R/R,q}$ is the identity under precisely these unit identifications.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; identity coefficient square and its mate

proof.text:
Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to the two squares $\mu^{S/R}:L_SC_{S/R,W}\to C_{S/R,Z}L_R$ and $\mu^{B/S}:L_BC_{B/S,W}\to C_{B/S,Z}L_S$. Their pasted square has mate
$$C_{B/S,W}C_{S/R,W}R_R\longrightarrow C_{B/S,W}R_SC_{S/R,Z}\longrightarrow R_BC_{B/S,Z}C_{S/R,Z},$$
whose forward composite is $\pi_{B/S,q,C_{S/R,Z}(-)}\,C_{B/S,W}(\pi_{S/R,q})$, by Step 4. Step 3 identifies the pasted left square with $\mu^{B/R}$ after $a_W,a_Z$. Naturality of the adjunction bijections [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] sends postcomposition of the transpose by $a_Z$ to postcomposition of the mate by $R_B(a_Z)$, and precomposition by $L_B(a_W^{-1})$ to precomposition by $a_W^{-1}$. Consequently
$$\pi_{B/R,q,M}=R_B(a_{Z,M})\,\pi_{B/S,q,C_{S/R,Z}M}\,C_{B/S,W}(\pi_{S/R,q,M})\,(a_{W,R_RM})^{-1}.$$
This mate calculation takes place throughout in the $B$-module categories. Scalar restriction was used only to detect invertibility in Step 6; no faithfulness of scalar restriction on derived Hom sets is used for this equality.
